alignments.note: Imperative rendered by the bare verb.

Negative subordinator after a verb of caution: the ASV writes 'that ... refuse not', so the complementizer and the negation both answer to it, discontinuously under rule 15, headed on the negation. Giving only 'not' to the particle and reading 'that' as an ordinary complementizer helper on the subjunctive is defensible, but rule 40 puts whatever word introduces the English clause on the subordinating element, and here that element is the negative particle itself.
Subject pronoun is the inflection's helper under rule 9; head on the lexical verb.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun and nothing else.
The participle carries the supplied relativizer under rule 32; head on the verb.
Ordinary conditional particle.
Postpositive conjunction rendered clause-initially.
Substantival demonstrative rendered by a bare pronoun; no article stands with it, so rule 49 is not in question.
Ordinary negative; no negative indefinite follows, so rules 41 and 59 do not apply.
Finite verb.
Preposition realized by 'on' under rule 36.
Anarthrous noun with no determiner in the ASV.

Circumstantial participle expanded into a finite clause: the supplied subordinator 'when' and subject 'they' are rule 7 helpers licensed by the participle itself (rule 86), headed on the lexical verb.
Substantival article before a participle: rule 32 gives it the pronoun alone.
Relativizer and the supplied object 'them' both ride with the participle, the object staying with the verb that requires it in English under rule 74; head on the verb.
Adverbial accusative of degree.
Comparative adverb.
Emphatic subject pronoun; the supplied verb around it is handled separately under rule 103.

The Greek apodosis is elliptical and expresses no verb: the ASV supplies 'shall not escape' by resuming the protasis, whose tokens are already spent — 'escaped' on s010 and 'not' on s009. Rule 103 makes such repeated lexical content 'added' rather than a rule 7 helper, and the supplied auxiliary and negation stay inside the unit. Reading the three words as a discontinuous second realization of s009 and s010 under rule 15 remains defensible.
Substantival article before a participle rendered by a single relativizer: rule 90 gives that one word to the article, the participle keeping its own verb.

The verb governs its object directly in Greek, so the supplied English 'from' is the verb's own particle rather than a preposition answering to a source token; 'away' likewise belongs to the English phrasal verb. Head on the lexical verb.

Article governing a prepositional phrase with no expressed head noun: rule 31's carve-out keeps the supplied relativizer on the article, discontinuously with its pronoun as in rule 32's 'they ... that are with him'.

The ASV supplies a finite 'warneth' for the verbless articular phrase, resuming s015, which is already spent on 'warned' at t019. Rule 103 makes such repeated lexical content 'added'. Rules 31 and 62 would instead fold a supplied verb onto the preposition ('warneth from' on s021), and that reading stays defensible — the ASV's own margin, 'that is from heaven', shows the phrase read as a bare copular one — but here the supplied verb is not a copula and its licensing token has already spent its English.
Preposition realized by 'from'; the ASV gives the governed noun no determiner, so nothing else rides here.
Plural Greek rendered by an English singular with no determiner.

review_notes: s002 takes both 'that' and 'not' as one discontinuous unit; the competing reading gives it only 'not'.
The two supplied English resumptions — 'shall not escape' and 'warneth' — are marked 'added' under rule 103, since s009, s010 and s015 are all spent earlier in the verse.
The three underdetermined variant units (v014, v015, v016) leave the projection carrying readings the ASV permits, so rule 97 is not in question and no textual decision is made here.
